sections.heading: The setup
sections.body: The S&P 500 closed Nov 19 at 7,176, its low for the past month and 7.5% under the Oct 21 high of 7,757; it fell 2.0% on the day. The Nasdaq 100 sits at 26,517, also at its 1-month low, down 11.1% from its high. The VIX closed at 28.4, its 1-month high, after rising 15.8% in one session from a month-ago reading of 18.4. The Euro Stoxx 50 held up better, at 6,114, 4.5% under its 1-month high. Earnings load is light: 18 names in the S&P 500, Russell 1000 and core pool report Nov 23-26, mostly technology (6) and consumer-cyclical (5) names, with 10 landing on Tuesday.

sections.heading: What to watch
sections.body: Monday: HPE, Zoom and Electronic Arts report, with HPE and Zoom in the technology group (median +0.2% off recent prints). Tuesday is the busiest day: Analog Devices, Workday, Nutanix and HP Inc. in technology, plus Best Buy, Burlington and Dick's in consumer-cyclical (median +0.3%), and Medtronic in healthcare (median -0.1%). Wednesday brings Deere (industrials, median +0.3%) and Bath & Body Works. Thursday has only Gap. All 18 dates in the pool are estimated rather than confirmed, so check company calendars.

sections.heading: Signals to trust
sections.body: The three sectors with the largest median 3-day reaction are mining (+4.6% median, 215 tickers, 2,766 news items), copper (-2.5%, 6 tickers, 231 news items) and energy (+2.0%, 315 tickers, 5,144 news items). Mining and energy have thick news windows (over 1,000 items); copper does not, and with 6 names its median rests on little. None of this week's 18 scheduled reporters sit in these three sectors, so the sector moves come from names that have already reported.
